Opening notes from triage:
- Observed a correlated surge in short, high-concurrency traffics hitting the hosted API in us-west-2 starting 07:40 PDT.
- Autoscaler (dedicated orchestrator) logged multiple back-to-back scale-down/scale-up cycles; there is an open bug where rapid scale flapping can cause connection churn and KV cache invalidation.
- We also saw an abnormal grouping of long ContextWindow requests that trigger larger KV cache entries and increase serialization time (affects tail latency).

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00):
1) Forced sticky routing to a stable pool to avoid the flapping nodes (short-term).
2) Temporarily increased min instances for the impacted model pool to reduce autoscaler oscillation.
3) Enabled aggressive KV cache warming for the checkout model.

Next actions / owners:
- Rishi to lead a root-cause analysis on autoscaler flapping and propose a config fix by EOD. (Owner: Rishi Malhotra)
- Marissa to coordinate an RCA draft and timeline for execution (Owner: Marissa Cole).
- Priya to coordinate customer comms and exec readout scheduling (Owner: Priya Natarajan).

I'll paste logs and a short timeline into the incident doc.

-Jordan

Amy / team —

Attached is our preliminary RCA draft (rca-draft-sapphire.docx). High-level summary below: 

Summary of root cause (preliminary):
- Primary cause: Autoscaler configuration bug that allowed rapid scale-down following brief traffic dips, leading to connection churn when instances rejoined and left the pool.
- Contributing factor: A recent inference runtime change (continuous batching heuristic tweak) increased KV cache churn for long-context checkout requests, amplifying tail latency under concurrent load.
- Result: Higher queueing and a ~4–5% increase in 500 errors during the spike window.

Corrective actions (with owners & ETA):
- P1 config fix to autoscaler to add damping window on scale-downs (Owner: Rishi Malhotra) — ETA: 24h for rollout to canary, 72h for full rollout.
- Revert/adjust continuous batching heuristic for the checkout model and add a targeted perf test (Owner: Eng Runtime Team / Rishi) — ETA: 48h.
- Implement proactive KV cache warming and persistent cold-start memoization for frequent checkout prefixes (Owner: Runtime Ops — Marissa) — ETA: 5 business days.
- Create a dedicated playbook for scale-flapping detection and automated mitigation (Owner: Grace O'Connor) — ETA: 7 business days.
- Customer remediation: one-time service credit and 2-week priority monitoring window (Owner: Priya) — to propose to Sapphire execs.

Request: Can Sapphire confirm whether the proposed credit and monitoring window are acceptable? Also propose a 30-minute exec readout tomorrow 09:00 PDT to walk through RCA and the cadence for weekly updates.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.com
